A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DART research work. All supplied pages, including appendices, are readable, and corresponding equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video benchmark results, inference-cost measurements, and analyses of pivot selection, pruning layers, and token modalities.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds training-time pruning, larger-model evaluations, speech-recognition experiments, and robot-manipulation simulations.

M1.justification: The pivot-selection and cosine-duplication pruning algorithm remains unchanged. v2 adds DART†, which applies DART during LLaVA-1.5-7B training rather than only during inference (Section 4.1, Table 1); no new architecture or loss is specified.

E1.justification: v2 adds automatic speech recognition on FLEURS-en and LibriSpeech-long, plus four SIMPLER robot-manipulation tasks under Visual Matching and Variant Aggregation (Appendix B, Tables 10–11). The original image and video benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: FitPrune is added to the LLaVA-1.5-7B comparisons at all three retention levels in Table 1. VLA-Cache is newly evaluated in SIMPLER Table 11. Existing image/video comparators remain; FiCoCo-V was already evaluated in v1 despite receiving additional documentation in v2.

E3.justification: v2 adds 13B/72B model configurations and evaluations of training-time DART. New protocols include 20%, 30%, and 50% audio-token reduction measured by Word Error Rate, and robot evaluations using 224×224 observations, task success rates, FLOPs, and speedup. The corresponding original image/video settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 and Figure 8 extend pivot-count sensitivity testing to POPE, SQA, MMBench, and GQA. Appendix B.2 adds robustness evaluation under SIMPLER variations in lighting, backgrounds, and surface textures. Existing pivot-selection, layer, modality, and sparsification analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 8 adds standard deviations and explicitly reports five different random seeds for random pivot selection; v1 Table 6 gives only point estimates. This establishes newly documented uncertainty reporting, without establishing an increase over v1's unspecified run count.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for larger models, speech recognition, robot manipulation, and pivot-count sensitivity. Table 1 adds training-time DART† averages of 100.4%, 99.9%, and 97.2% at 192/128/64 tokens; the original inference-only averages remain 98.8%, 98.0%, and 93.7%, so these are separate settings. Original efficiency and image/video scores are otherwise retained, while ToMe's 88.5%, 80.4%, and 70.1% averages are removed.

T1.justification: The pivot and duplication definitions, Lipschitz and bounded-embedding assumptions, lemmas, performance-bound proof, and FLOPs derivation are retained. v2 adds only a prose summary of the existing theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the same central claims about duplication-based, training-free pruning and efficient-attention compatibility, including the 88.9% pruning and 1.99×/2.99× speedup figures. The conclusion preserves the main performance, token-subset, and hallucination claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning scalability and applicability to audio and robotic control. Section 7 removes v1's substantive limitation that pruning is less effective for information-dense tokens, including its explanations involving Qwen2-VL merging and MiniCPM's resampler. The black-box-access limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link, checkpoint links for newly evaluated models, and technical settings for audio and robot experiments. The hardware/software specification remains unchanged. The DART† training recipe is not detailed.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands research context into audio models and vision-language-action systems in Appendix B. It also discusses DTMFormer and MADTP in related work, adds FitPrune and FiCoCo documentation, and cites prior work motivating training-time pruning. The central positioning around duplication remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 condenses related work, the main-results discussion, efficiency analysis, and conclusion, and rewrites the limitations section. It adds an appendix contents list and task-specific dataset subsections. Most introductory and methodological prose and the main section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 1, separates its existing LLaVA-Next block into Table 3, and adds Tables 7 and 9–11 plus the four-panel Figure 8. Several existing displays move or change numbering; the original final sparsification visualization is retained as Figure 9.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support for scalability and pruning robustness through 13B/72B evaluations, additional pivot-count tests, five-seed uncertainty reporting, and audio and robot evaluations that include visual perturbations. These test important aspects of generality and stability beyond v1's evidence. Removing the information-density limitation and leaving DART† training underspecified weaken transparency, but the net gain in empirical support is substantial.
